title: 15. System Design Case Studies: Design E-commerce Platform
summary: Design a large-scale e-commerce platform (Amazon / Flipkart / Shopify style) supporting product catalog, full-text search, cart, checkout, order management, inventory, payments, recommendations, and reviews at 100 M users with…

sections.title: Step 1: Clarify Requirements (5 min)
sections.body:
> **In one line:** Design a large-scale e-commerce platform (Amazon / Flipkart / Shopify style) supporting product catalog, full-text search, cart, checkout, order management, inventory, payments, recommendations, and reviews at 100 M users with Black Friday traffic spikes (10× baseline). ---

### Functional Requirements
- **Product catalog**: 100 M+ products, each with title, description, attributes (color, size, brand), images, price, category, variants (parent/child SKUs).
- **Search**: full-text search with filters (price range, brand, rating, prime-eligible), sort (relevance, price, popularity, newest), autocomplete, typo tolerance. Response < 200 ms p99.
- **Product detail page**: images, description, specs, variants, reviews, related products, "customers also bought". Page render < 500 ms p99.
- **Cart**: add/remove/update quantity, persists across devices (logged-in users), 30-day TTL for guest carts, supports 100 items max.
- **Checkout**: address selection, payment method, coupon/promo code, tax calculation, shipping method, order review, place order. Idempotent order placement.
- **Inventory**: real-time stock count per SKU; atomic decrement on order placement; restock; reservation during checkout (5-minute hold).
- **Order management**: order lifecycle (`created → paid → fulfilled → shipped → delivered → returned / cancelled`); order history; tracking.
- **Payments**: integrate payment gateway (Stripe/PayPal); support saved cards, wallets, BNPL; refunds.
- **Recommendations**: personalized home page, "frequently bought together", "customers also viewed"; updated based on user behavior.
- **Reviews & ratings**: 1–5 star rating + text review, photo/video uploads, helpful votes, verified-purchase badge, moderation.
- **Seller portal**: sellers manage products, inventory, pricing, orders, settlement reports.
- **Notifications**: order confirmation, shipping updates, delivery, price-drop alerts via email/SMS/push.

### Non-Functional Requirements
- **Availability** 99.99 % for browsing/checkout; 99.95 % for recommendations (degrade gracefully).
- **Latency**: search p99 < 200 ms; PDP p99 < 500 ms; checkout p99 < 1 s; order placement p99 < 2 s.
- **Scale**: 100 M MAU, 50 M DAU, 5 M concurrent peak (Black Friday). 5 B page views/day baseline, 50 B on Black Friday. 10 M orders/day baseline, 30 M on Black Friday peak.
- **Black Friday**: traffic 10× baseline for 4 hours; 20× peak flash-sale bursts; no degradation of checkout.
- **Durability**: orders and payments never lost (Kafka + replicated DB); at-least-once processing.
- **Consistency**: per-SKU inventory is linearizable (no overselling); cart is eventually consistent across devices < 5 s.
- **Search relevance**: must handle synonyms, misspellings, multi-lingual (10+ languages for global platform).

### Back-of-Envelope Estimation
- **Catalog**: 100 M products × 5 KB metadata + 10 images × 100 KB = ~105 TB metadata + 100 TB images = 205 TB hot. Index size in ES: ~2× metadata = 1 TB.
- **Search QPS**: 50 M DAU × 20 searches/day = 1 B searches/day ≈ 12 k/s avg, 120 k/s Black Friday peak.
- **PDP QPS**: 5 B page views/day → 60 k/s avg, 600 k/s peak. Each PDP renders 1 product + 5 related → 6 product lookups per view.
- **Cart**: 50 M users with active cart avg 5 items → 250 M cart-item rows. 100 ops/s on cart per active user.
- **Orders**: 10 M orders/day × 5 items avg = 50 M inventory decrements/day. Peak: 50 k orders/s on Black Friday.
- **Payments**: 10 M orders/day = $1 B daily volume (avg ticket $100). Peak 50 k tx/s → payment gateway must handle.
- **Inventory**: 100 M SKUs × 10 warehouses = 1 B inventory rows; read-heavy (every PDP) + write-heavy on checkout.
- **CDN**: 100 TB images at 5 B views/day → 500 PB/month egress → CDN is mandatory; origin only for cache misses.

### Scope
In scope: catalog, search, PDP, cart, checkout, order, inventory, payments, reviews, recommendations, notifications. Out of scope: seller onboarding/KYC, logistics/shipping carrier integration, returns processing, marketing campaigns, A/B testing platform.

sections.title: Step 2: High-Level Architecture (10 min)
sections.body:
### Components 1. **Edge CDN** (CloudFront / Akamai): caches static assets (images, JS, CSS) and edge-caches PDP HTML for popular products. Origin shield reduces load on app tier. 2. **API Gateway**: REST + GraphQL; rate limit per user/IP; auth via JWT; WAF. 3. **BFF (Backend for Frontend)** per client: web BFF, mobile BFF, seller BFF — orchestrates microservice calls and shapes responses. 4. **Catalog Service**: CRUD for products; Postgres sharded by `product_id`; read replicas for browse. 5. **Search Service**: Elasticsearch cluster (100 nodes); index from Catalog CDC; relevance tuned with synonyms, boost factors. 6. **PDP Service**: assembles product detail page from catalog, inventory, reviews, recommendations; server-side rendered and edge-cached. 7. **Cart Service**: Redis-backed cart per user (logged-in) or session (guest); 30-day TTL; syncs to Postgres for persistence. 8. **Inventory Service**: per-SKU-per-warehouse stock; atomic decrement via Redis Lua script + Postgres durable; reservation with 5-min TTL. 9. **Checkout Service**: orchestrates cart → address → payment → order placement; idempotent via `idempotency_key`. 10. **Order Service**: order state machine; Kafka events for downstream (inventory decrement, payment, shipping). 11. **Payment Service**: integrates with Payment Gateway (Topic 14); tokenized cards; idempotent. 12. **Recommendation Service**: collaborative filtering + content-based; pre-computed top-N per user in Redis; updated daily via Spark. 13. **Review Service**: ratings + reviews; moderation queue; helpful-vote aggregation. 14. **Notification Service**: Kafka events → email/SMS/push (Topic 12). 15. **Storage**: Postgres (sharded) for catalog/orders/payments; Redis for cart/inventory hot data/recommendations; Elasticsearch for search; S3 for images; Snowflake/Redshift for analytics. ### Mermaid Diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD User[User: Web / Mobile] --> CDN[CDN
CloudFront / Akamai] CDN -->|cache miss| BFF[BFF Web / Mobile / Seller] BFF --> AGW[API Gateway / GraphQL] AGW --> CAT[Catalog Service] AGW --> SRH[Search Service
Elasticsearch] AGW --> PDP[PDP Service
catalog + inv + reviews + reco] AGW --> CART[Cart Service
Redis + Postgres] AGW --> CHK[Checkout Service] CHK --> INV[Inventory Service
Redis Lua + Postgres] CHK --> PAY[Payment Service
-> Payment Gateway] CHK --> ORD[Order Service] ORD --> K[(Kafka: order.events)] K --> INV K --> NOT[Notification Service] K --> SHIP[Shipping Service] K --> AN[Analytics / Snowflake] PDP --> REC[Recommendation Service
Redis top-N per user] CAT -->|CDC| SRH CAT -->|CDC| REC Review[Review Service] --> PDP Seller[Seller Portal] --> AGW CAT --> S3[(S3: product images
+ CDN)] ``` ### ASCII Diagram ``` +----------+ CDN (cache images, PDP HTML) +-----------+ | User | ---------------------------------------> | Edge CDN | | web/mob | <--- static assets, cached PDP --------- | | +----+-----+ +-----+------+ | | | cache miss | v v +----+----------+ orchestrate +--------+ +-------+-------+ | BFF (web/mob/ | --------------> | API | <-----> | Catalog Svc | | seller) | | Gateway| | (Postgres) | +---------------+ +---+----+ +---------------+ | +------------+----------+-------+-------+----------+ v v v v v +----+---+ +-----+----+ +---+-----+ +-------+--+ +---+----+ | Search | | PDP | | Cart | | Checkout | | Review | | (ES) | |assemble | | (Redis) | | | +--------+ +--------+ |cat+inv+ | +---------+ +----+-----+ |rev+reco | | +----------+ v +-------+------+ | Inventory | -- Redis Lua (atomic decrement) | Service | -- Postgres (durable) +-------+------+ ^ | reserve / commit | +-------+------+ places order | Payment | -----------------> Payment Gateway | Service | <----------------- (Stripe) +-------+------+ | v +-------+------+ produces | Order Service| ----------------> Kafka order.events +--------------+ | +--> Inventory (decrement) +--> Notification (email/SMS/push) +--> Shipping (carrier API) +--> Analytics (Snowflake) ``` ### Request Flow Walkthrough 1. User searches "wireless headphones" → BFF → API Gateway → Search Service (Elasticsearch) returns 50 results + facets in 150 ms. 2. User clicks a product → CDN serves cached PDP HTML if popular (cache hit ~70 %); cache miss → PDP Service assembles from Catalog (Postgres) + Inventory (Redis) + Reviews (Postgres read replica) + Recommendations (Redis) → renders HTML → CDN caches for 60 s. 3. User clicks "Add to Cart" → API Gateway → Cart Service → Redis `LPUSH cart:{user_id} {sku, qty}` → syncs to Postgres async → returns 200. 4. User opens cart → Cart Service reads from Redis, validates prices against Catalog (price may have changed), shows cart. 5. User clicks "Checkout" → Checkout Service creates a checkout session; reserves inventory for each item (Redis Lua atomic decrement with 5-min TTL); shows address + payment UI. 6. User selects address + saved card → clicks "Place Order" → Checkout Service: (a) re-validates inventory reservation, (b) calls Payment Service → Payment Gateway captures funds, (c) creates Order in Postgres (status=paid), (d) commits inventory decrement (Redis reservation → Postgres durable), (e) clears cart, (f) produces `order.created` event to Kafka. 7. Kafka consumers: Inventory Service updates stock counts; Notification Service sends order-confirmation email/SMS/push; Shipping Service allocates to nearest warehouse and creates shipping label; Analytics streams to Snowflake. 8. Order tracking: user queries order status; Order Service reads from Postgres + subscribes to shipping carrier webhooks for status updates. 9. Reviews: user submits review → Review Service stores in Postgres, queues for moderation, recalculates product rating average asynchronously. 10. Recommendations: nightly Spark job processes user behavior (views, purchases, cart adds) → collaborative filtering model → writes top-50 recommended products per user to Redis → home page reads from Redis.

sections.title: Step 3: Deep Dive — Data Model (10 min)
sections.body:
### Tables / Schema

```sql
-- Product catalog (Postgres, Citus-distributed by product_id)
CREATE TABLE products (
    product_id    BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,        -- snowflake
    parent_id     BIGINT,                    -- for variants
    title         TEXT NOT NULL,
    description   TEXT,
    brand         TEXT,
    category_id   BIGINT NOT NULL,
    attributes    JSONB,                     -- {color: red, size: M, weight: 1.2kg}
    base_price    NUMERIC(10,2) NOT NULL,    -- DECIMAL not float
    currency      CHAR(3) DEFAULT 'USD',
    is_active     BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
    created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE product_images (
    image_id    BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    product_id  BIGINT NOT NULL,
    s3_key      TEXT NOT NULL,
    cdn_url     TEXT NOT NULL,
    sort_order  INT,
    width       INT, height INT
);

CREATE TABLE inventory (
    sku_id        BIGINT NOT NULL,            -- = product_id for variants
    warehouse_id  INT NOT NULL,
    stock_qty     INT NOT NULL,
    reserved_qty  INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,     -- held during checkout
    version       BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,  -- optimistic lock
    updated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (sku_id, warehouse_id)
);

-- Cart is primarily Redis; Postgres is durable backup for cross-device sync
CREATE TABLE cart_items (
    user_id      BIGINT NOT NULL,
    sku_id       BIGINT NOT NULL,
    quantity     INT NOT NULL,
    added_at     TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (user_id, sku_id)
);

CREATE TABLE orders (
    order_id       BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id        BIGINT NOT NULL,
    status         TEXT NOT NULL,             -- created|paid|fulfilled|shipped|delivered|cancelled|returned
    subtotal       NUMERIC(10,2),
    tax            NUMERIC(10,2),
    shipping       NUMERIC(10,2),
    discount       NUMERIC(10,2),
    total          NUMERIC(10,2) NOT NULL,
    currency       CHAR(3),
    shipping_addr  JSONB,
    payment_id     TEXT,                      -- from Payment Gateway
    idempotency_key TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at     TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at     TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE order_items (
    order_id      BIGINT NOT NULL,
    sku_id        BIGINT NOT NULL,
    quantity      INT NOT NULL,
    unit_price    NUMERIC(10,2) NOT NULL,     -- snapshot at order time
    warehouse_id  INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (order_id, sku_id)
);

CREATE TABLE reviews (
    review_id    BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    product_id   BIGINT NOT NULL,
    user_id      BIGINT NOT NULL,
    rating       SMALLINT NOT NULL,           -- 1-5
    title        TEXT,
    body         TEXT,
    verified_purchase BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
    helpful_votes INT DEFAULT 0,
    status       TEXT DEFAULT 'pending',      -- pending|approved|rejected
    created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE product_ratings (
    product_id    BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    avg_rating    NUMERIC(2,1),               -- 4.3
    rating_count  INT,                        -- distribution
    rating_1      INT, rating_2 INT, rating_3 INT, rating_4 INT, rating_5 INT,
    updated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

-- Redis keys:
--   cart:{user_id}              -> HASH {sku_id: qty}
--   inv:{sku_id}                -> HASH {warehouse_id: stock_qty - reserved_qty}
--   inv_reserve:{checkout_id}   -> HASH {sku_id: qty}  (TTL 5 min)
--   reco:{user_id}              -> ZSET [product_id, score]  (top-50)
--   search_autocomplete:{prefix}-> LIST of suggestions (TTL 1h)
--   pdp_cache:{product_id}      -> rendered HTML (TTL 60s)
--   price:{sku_id}              -> cached base_price
```

### Indexes
- `products (category_id, base_price)` — category browse.
- `products (brand)` — brand filter.
- `products GIN (attributes)` — JSONB attribute filter.
- `products (title)` trigram index — fallback for SQL LIKE (when ES is down).
- `inventory (sku_id)` — primary key covers, but `(sku_id, warehouse_id)` lookup for multi-warehouse allocation.
- `orders (user_id, created_at DESC)` — order history.
- `reviews (product_id, status, helpful_votes DESC)` — show top approved reviews.
- `product_ratings (avg_rating DESC)` — top-rated browse.
- Elasticsearch: inverted index on `title` + `description`, with boost on `title`; aggregations on `brand`, `category`, `attributes.color`, `base_price` ranges.

### Storage Choice
- **Postgres + Citus** for catalog/orders/reviews — distributed by `product_id` (catalog) and `user_id` (orders). ACID for orders is non-negotiable.
- **Redis Cluster** for cart, inventory hot counts, recommendations, session. ~10 TB across 30 shards.
- **Elasticsearch** (100 nodes, ~1 TB index) for search; one replica per shard for HA; daily index refresh.
- **S3 + CDN** for product images — never serve from origin.
- **Snowflake / Redshift** for analytics — daily ETL via Kafka → S3 → Snowpipe.
- **DynamoDB** (alternative): for cart (key-value access pattern is perfect); we use Redis for low-latency reads but DynamoDB is a valid choice.

sections.title: Step 4: Deep Dive — Key Algorithms & APIs (10 min)
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- local checkout_id = KEYS[1] local items = cjson.decode(ARGV[1]) -- [{sku_id, qty, warehouse_id}] local ttl = tonumber(ARGV[2]) local reserved = {}…
- Inventory reservation with atomic decrement via Redis Lua script.
- Critical: NEVER oversell. Use Redis CAS (compare-and-swap) in Lua.
- Atomic batch reservation: either all succeed or all fail.
- Convert reservation to permanent decrement: Redis reserved -= qty, Postgres -= qty.
- Redis: remove from reserved (the stock was already deducted from available)
- Cancel reservation (user abandoned checkout). Restore available.
- Idempotent checkout: place order only once per idempotency_key.

**Defines:** `InventoryService`, `CheckoutService`

### API Design

```
# Catalog
GET    /v1/products?category=&brand=&sort=&page=    -> list
GET    /v1/products/{id}                            -> PDP payload
POST   /v1/products                                 -> seller creates (admin auth)

# Search
GET    /v1/search?q=wireless+headphones&filters=&sort=&page=
GET    /v1/search/autocomplete?q=wire

# Cart
POST   /v1/cart/items                  { sku_id, quantity }
PATCH  /v1/cart/items/{sku_id}         { quantity }
DELETE /v1/cart/items/{sku_id}
GET    /v1/cart

# Checkout
POST   /v1/checkout                    { cart_version, shipping_addr, payment_method }
                                      -> { checkout_id, expires_at, total }
POST   /v1/checkout/{id}/place         { idempotency_key }   -> { order_id }

# Orders
GET    /v1/orders?status=&from=&to=
GET    /v1/orders/{id}
POST   /v1/orders/{id}/cancel

# Reviews
POST   /v1/products/{id}/reviews       { rating, title, body }
GET    /v1/products/{id}/reviews?sort=helpful&page=
POST   /v1/reviews/{id}/helpful

# Recommendations
GET    /v1/recommendations?user_id=&context=home|pdp|cart
```

### Key Algorithms

```python
# Inventory reservation with atomic decrement via Redis Lua script.
# Critical: NEVER oversell. Use Redis CAS (compare-and-swap) in Lua.
RESERVE_LUA = """
local checkout_id = KEYS[1]
local items = cjson.decode(ARGV[1])    -- [{sku_id, qty, warehouse_id}]
local ttl = tonumber(ARGV[2])
local reserved = {}
for _, item in ipairs(items) do
    local key = "inv:" .. item.sku_id .. ":" .. item.warehouse_id
    local avail = tonumber(redis.call("HGET", key, "available")) or 0
    if avail < item.qty then
        -- Rollback any prior reservations in this batch
        for _, r in ipairs(reserved) do
            redis.call("HINCRBY", "inv:"..r.sku_id..":"..r.warehouse_id, "available", r.qty)
            redis.call("HINCRBY", "inv:"..r.sku_id..":"..r.warehouse_id, "reserved", -r.qty)
        end
        return {err = "insufficient_stock", sku = item.sku_id, requested = item.qty, available = avail}
    end
    redis.call("HINCRBY", key, "available", -item.qty)
    redis.call("HINCRBY", key, "reserved", item.qty)
    table.insert(reserved, {sku_id=item.sku_id, warehouse_id=item.warehouse_id, qty=item.qty})
end
-- Store the reservation for commit/rollback
redis.call("HSET", "inv_reserve:"..checkout_id, "items", cjson.encode(reserved))
redis.call("EXPIRE", "inv_reserve:"..checkout_id, ttl)
return {ok = "reserved", count = #reserved}
"""

class InventoryService:
    def __init__(self, redis, postgres):
        self.r, self.pg = redis, postgres
        self._reserve = self.r.register_script(RESERVE_LUA)

    async def reserve(self, checkout_id, items, ttl_seconds=300):
        # Atomic batch reservation: either all succeed or all fail.
        result = await self._reserve(keys=[checkout_id],
                                      args=[json.dumps(items), ttl_seconds])
        if result.get("err") == "insufficient_stock":
            raise InsufficientStockError(result["sku"], result["requested"], result["available"])
        return result

    async def commit(self, checkout_id, order_id):
        # Convert reservation to permanent decrement: Redis reserved -= qty, Postgres -= qty.
        items = json.loads(await self.r.hget(f"inv_reserve:{checkout_id}", "items"))
        async with self.pg.tx() as tx:
            for item in items:
                await tx.execute(
                    "UPDATE inventory SET stock_qty = stock_qty - $1, reserved_qty = "
                    "reserved_qty - $1, version = version + 1, updated_at = now() "
                    "WHERE sku_id = $2 AND warehouse_id = $3",
                    item["qty"], item["sku_id"], item["warehouse_id"])
                # Redis: remove from reserved (the stock was already deducted from available)
                await self.r.hincrby(f"inv:{item['sku_id']}:{item['warehouse_id']}",
                                     "reserved", -item["qty"])
        await self.r.delete(f"inv_reserve:{checkout_id}")

    async def release(self, checkout_id):
        # Cancel reservation (user abandoned checkout). Restore available.
        items = json.loads(await self.r.hget(f"inv_reserve:{checkout_id}", "items") or "[]")
        for item in items:
            await self.r.hincrby(f"inv:{item['sku_id']}:{item['warehouse_id']}",
                                 "available", item["qty"])
            await self.r.hincrby(f"inv:{item['sku_id']}:{item['warehouse_id']}",
                                 "reserved", -item["qty"])
        await self.r.delete(f"inv_reserve:{checkout_id}")
```

```python
# Idempotent checkout: place order only once per idempotency_key.
class CheckoutService:
    def __init__(self, idem_redis, inventory, payment, order_svc, cart_svc):
        self.idem, self.inv, self.pay, self.ord, self.cart = idem_redis, inventory, payment, order_svc, cart_svc

    async def place_order(self, user_id, checkout_id, idem_key):
        # 1. Idempotency check
        cached = await self.idem.get(f"idem:order:{user_id}:{idem_key}")
        if cached:
            return json.loads(cached)        # return original response

        lock = await self.idem.set(f"lock:order:{user_id}:{idem_key}", "1", nx=True, ex=600)
        if not lock:
            return {"status": "processing"}

        try:
            # 2. Re-validate reservation is still alive
            reserve = await self.idem.exists(f"inv_reserve:{checkout_id}")
            if not reserve:
                return {"status": "failed", "reason": "reservation_expired"}

            # 3. Capture payment
            cart = await self.cart.get(user_id)
            pay_result = await self.pay.capture(user_id, cart.total, idem_key)
            if pay_result.status != "succeeded":
                await self.inv.release(checkout_id)
                return self._cache(user_id, idem_key, {"status": "payment_failed"})

            # 4. Create order + commit inventory in one DB transaction
            order_id = snowflake_id()
            async with self.ord.tx() as tx:
                await tx.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO orders(order_id,user_id,status,total,currency,"
                    "payment_id,idempotency_key,created_at) VALUES($1,$2,'paid',$3,$4,$5,$6,now())",
                    order_id, user_id, cart.total, cart.currency, pay_result.payment_id, idem_key)
                for item in cart.items:
                    await tx.execute(
                        "INSERT INTO order_items(order_id,sku_id,quantity,unit_price,warehouse_id) "
                        "VALUES($1,$2,$3,$4,$5)", order_id, item.sku_id, item.quantity,
                        item.unit_price, item.warehouse_id)
            # 5. Commit inventory (Redis reservation -> Postgres decrement)
            await self.inv.commit(checkout_id, order_id)
            # 6. Clear cart, emit event
            await self.cart.clear(user_id)
            await self.kafka.send("order.events", {"type": "order.created",
                                                   "order_id": order_id, "user_id": user_id})
            return self._cache(user_id, idem_key, {"status": "success", "order_id": order_id})
        except Exception as e:
            await self.pay.refund(idem_key)   # rollback payment
            await self.inv.release(checkout_id)
            return self._cache(user_id, idem_key, {"status": "failed", "reason": str(e)})
```

sections.title: Step 5: Scalability & Reliability (5 min)
sections.body:
### Scaling Challenges
- **Search at 120k QPS peak**: Elasticsearch cluster of 100 nodes (50 data, 30 coordinator, 20 ingest). Index sharded 30 ways × 2 replicas. Hot searches cached in Redis (top 10k queries). Autocomplete uses a smaller in-memory trie (Redis).
- **PDP at 600k QPS peak**: 70 % CDN cache hit for popular products; cold-cache fallback assembles from Postgres read replicas (10 read replicas). The PDP service is stateless and auto-scales to 1000 instances.
- **Inventory hotspots**: a viral product can have 100k concurrent checkouts. The Redis Lua script handles atomic decrement, but a single key is limited to ~10k ops/s. We shard inventory by warehouse (10 warehouses) — each warehouse key is independent, raising effective throughput to 100k ops/s. If still hot, we shard by `(sku, warehouse, shard_id)` and aggregate.
- **Checkout atomicity**: place-order must be atomic across inventory + payment + order. We use a saga with compensating transactions (refund payment if order fails; release inventory if payment fails). Idempotency key on the whole checkout ensures retries don't double-charge.
- **Black Friday surge 10×**: pre-warm CDN with top 10k products; pre-scale app tier to 2× normal; provision extra Kafka partitions; pre-warm Redis with inventory; rate-limit non-essential traffic (recommendations, recommendations, reviews) to protect checkout.
- **Image egress 500 PB/month**: CDN is mandatory; origin shield (single region) reduces cross-region traffic; image resizing at edge (CloudFront Lambda@Edge) eliminates origin hits for resize variants.

### Caching Strategy
- **Multi-layer PDP cache**: CDN (60 s, HTML) → Redis (rendered JSON, 5 min) → Postgres. Hit ratio target 90 %+.
- **Search cache**: Redis caches top 10k search results for 60 s; miss goes to ES.
- **Inventory cache**: Redis is the source of truth for hot path (atomic decrement); Postgres is durable backup; periodic reconciliation.
- **Price cache**: Redis per `sku_id`; updated on seller price change via pub/sub; cart reads from cache.
- **Recommendations**: pre-computed top-50 per user in Redis; refreshed nightly by Spark job.
- **Category tree**: cached in Redis, invalidated on category admin change.

### Failure Modes
- **Elasticsearch down**: search falls back to Postgres trigram indexes (slower, 1 s vs 200 ms) for the top 100k products only. Banner: "Search is degraded."
- **Redis (inventory) down**: circuit-break; pause checkout; show "checkout temporarily unavailable" rather than risk overselling. Read from Postgres `inventory` table directly (slower, but consistent).
- **Payment Gateway down**: Checkout Service returns `503` with `Retry-After`; cart is preserved; inventory reservation extended (TTL refreshed every minute). When gateway recovers, users retry.
- **Postgres primary down (orders shard)**: failover to replica (RPO < 1 s, RTO < 30 s); in-flight transactions rolled back; idempotency cache ensures retries succeed.
- **CDN origin shield down**: CDN continues serving from edge cache (TTL-stale accepted); new cache misses go directly to origin (load spike). Pre-warm via CloudFront invalidations once shield recovers.
- **Kafka broker down**: RF=3, min ISR=2; producers get acks=all so no data loss; consumers pause and resume on rebalance.
- **Recommendation service down**: home page shows default recommendations (top-selling categories) — graceful degradation.
